research_question: In adults with coronary heart disease, heart failure, or atrial fibrillation, what is the effect of a psychological intervention compared with no psychological intervention on depression symptoms at 6 to 12 months follow-up?
treatment_label: Psychological intervention (alone, with cardiac rehabilitation, or with pharmacotherapy)
control_label: No psychological intervention (usual care, attention control, or waitlist)
outcome_description: Depression symptom severity assessed via validated continuous depression instruments (e.g., BDI, BDI-II, BDI-FS, CDS, HADS-D, HAM-D, PHQ-9, ZDS) at 6 to 12 months follow-up
positive_direction: Higher depression symptom severity scores in the psychological intervention group compared to the control group
search_queries: psychological intervention coronary heart disease depression randomized trial
cognitive behavioral therapy heart failure depression controlled trial
psychological intervention atrial fibrillation depression outcomes comparison
inclusion_criteria: Adults diagnosed with coronary heart disease, heart failure, or atrial fibrillation
Evaluation of a psychological intervention (alone, combined with cardiac rehabilitation, or combined with pharmacotherapy) compared against no psychological intervention
Reports quantitative validated depression symptom scores at follow-up (6 to 12 months post-randomisation)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between a psychological intervention and a non-psychological control group
No quantitative depression outcome data reporting means, standard deviations, change scores, or test statistics suitable for calculating an effect size
Completely unrelated to the target cardiovascular populations (coronary heart disease, heart failure, or atrial fibrillation) or psychological interventions
moderators_to_extract: Cardiovascular condition (coronary heart disease, heart failure, atrial fibrillation)
Psychological intervention modality (cognitive behavioural therapy, mindfulness, supportive/counselling, other)
Co-intervention status (psychological alone, with cardiac rehabilitation, with pharmacotherapy)
Follow-up duration (in months, within the 6 to 12 month window)
effect_size_note: Standardized mean difference (SMD) pooled across validated depression instruments using the longest available follow-up between 6 and 12 months. Note that a negative effect size indicates greater reduction in depressive symptoms favoring the psychological intervention.
